If I understand the testimony well, it explains to us that the Serbs living in Bosnia and Herzegovina very much feared to lose their links with Serbia because they feared that a new confederative structure, or even independence of Bosnia and Herzegovina, would separate these Bosnian and Herzegovinian Serbs from the Serbs in Serbia and that they would be in a minority position in such a confederative or even independent Bosnia and Herzegovina and that this caused a lot of concern and that the SDS was very much opposed against such a development to take place. Mr. Treanor, I hope that I well understood your testimony in this respect.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that's a fair summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. To what extent is this in dispute, I would like to ask the Defence. If not, Mr. Tieger, we could have gone through it -- of course, I couldn't have invented the summary before hearing the testimony, but perhaps Mr. Treanor could have summarised it in this way and then we would be informed. And therefore, I'd like to ask

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: To what extent what we heard over the last hour is disputed, as summarised by me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, there's certainly the summary that --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Sorry. The summary that Your Honour has just given appears to me to be entirely accurate and not in dispute. I think I would be slightly hesitant to say that everything over the last hour is not in dispute. That's a rather --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but of course if there would be specific points that were in dispute, perhaps then they could have called some additional attention in the presentation of this evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. What I would say, Your Honour, is this: That despite our objections earlier status in the trial as to the forming, which questions are put in leading questions, when it comes to this sort of area, Mr. Tieger, I think having probably a pretty clear idea of the sort of areas where there isn't likely to be any serious dispute could, certainly as far as the Defence is concerned, lead the witness quite quickly through that sort of area, which is not seriously in dispute. So if that speeds things up -- Your Honour won't have objections from us in relation to matters which are simply either common knowledge or very clear and not in dispute. I think that's probably the most I can say as a practical help, Your Honour, because clearly I can't give blanket agreement to a huge chunk of evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not asking anyone to give a blanket agreement. But after this approximately one hour, I wondered whether we could not have gone through it a bit more quickly without having any difficulties between the parties. And there's always a risk that discussions on whether you could speed up do not take more time than the time you could gain. So I now leave it to the parties, but could you please keep this in the back of your mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour. If I may make one brief point. And certainly understand the Court's point. I would note, however, that embedded within statements concerning the apprehensions of Serbs in the area, as the Court described, are foreshadowing of responses that are threatened or that may be taken. That is an area that is somewhat distinct from perhaps the less controversial point about the concerns generated by the possibility of the disintegration of Yugoslavia. But I will be -- when it comes to the prospect of leading us through those portions, I will bear that distinction in mind and take advantage of counsel's point with respect to leading questions in the specific area he mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Finally, Mr. Treanor, if I could ask you to just focus on the last comment in the -- at the rally by Mr. Karadzic, which is found at page 6 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is at the top of the page, before the -- the heading further down the page. Dr. Karadzic is quoted as saying: "The more Yugoslavia's chances drop, the higher the chances of a Greater Serbia will be. All Serbs and a majority of the Muslims would vote for Serbia. We are the only people in Europe at this moment fighting against fascism, and our weapons are truth and justice." The reference to fascism I take to be a reference to the government of the HDZ in Croatia, which Serbian nationalist leaders tended to brand as being a continuation of the independent state of Croatia from the World War II era, that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor -- I'm sorry. Is there a further point you wanted to make about --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think we only have perhaps one more document on this particular issue and then we're moving to a different topic, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps we could move on in this way, Mr. Treanor, if we may. You spoke of references to -- or you identified references to single villages being -- not being left out of Yugoslavia, to the concern that we spoke of just recently of the Serbs and the SDS, about all Serbs remaining within Yugoslavia. Did the SDS begin to undertake steps, concrete steps, or proposals, to identify areas within Bosnia that were deemed to be Serb and that would not be removed from Yugoslavia under any circumstances?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I guess I was mistaken. There are two more documents. This one has come out of chronological order. This document is dated the 23rd of February, 1991, which is before the debate in the Assembly on the draft decision took place. So it was produced at the height of that controversy, if I can put it that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Treanor. For the benefit of Court and for the Chamber, that document from February 23rd may be found at tab 19. Mr. Treanor, does this document consider the possibility of Serbian municipalities undertaking steps to remain within Yugoslavia in the event of decisions by the Bosnian government which threatened the independence of Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the most extensive, certainly, and most concrete approach to what the leaders of the SDS contemplated as a possible line of action should something like the decision on sovereignty be passed and that lead, in fact, to the separation of BH from Yugoslavia. They had said before that they won't -- wouldn't recognise a decision, that sort of thing. They had spoken of the possibility of civil war as well. But here we see concrete administrative actions being contemplated should the republic government, as is put in this document, cease to function, and that is, no longer function in what the SDS would regard as a legal manner, that is, no longer within the framework of Yugoslavia. So we have a passage here highlighted at the bottom of page 2 or 3 of the translation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. That would be -- yes. That would be page 2 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which states that: "In order to provide for the unobstructed functioning of the municipality in such a situation, that is, when the republic government stops acting legally, in their view, as well as for the exercise of the aforementioned rights and obligations, the municipality must pass an appropriate legal document decision by which it would proclaim that from the moment when such a document is passed, the municipality's territory is an integral and indivisible part of Yugoslavia, that in its area, only federal laws adapted to this situation have legal effect. That it recognises the exclusive authority of the federal organs, the SFRY Assembly, the SFRY Presidency, the federal Executive Council, the JNA, security services, judicial organs, and so on, in the area it covers. This action would suspend the implementation of republican regulations in the areas of municipalities where such a document was passed, and at the same time, it would give legitimacy to the activities and measures undertaken by the federal organs." I think we're on a new page now, or new paragraph: "This would create a legal foundation for direct communication, such as assistance, cooperation, and the like, between these municipalities and the Federation, and its organs, the SFRY Assembly, Presidency, the federal Executive Council, et cetera, and through them, this would provide particularly for the need to engage the Yugoslav People's Army, the federal secretary for National Defence, the federal secretariat of the interior, the federal judicial organs," et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, may I again ask you a question, just to better understand the Prosecution's case. Your question was whether this document considered the possibility of Serbian municipalities undertaking steps in the event of decisions by the Bosnian government which threatened the independence of Bosnia. From what I understood now is that steps had to be taken if decisions would promote the independence of Bosnia, or is this a misunderstanding?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It was a poorly worded question, Your Honour, and I should have framed it as "threatened the prospect of an independent Bosnia." It might have been clearer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Perhaps I should ask whether the witness understood it in that manner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, perhaps from his answer he was mainly referring to the document rather than answering your question, I would say. But he explained what the document said. But it's -- I do understand that you understood the question of Mr. Tieger to be what steps to be taken if decisions would be taken unfavourable to the -- what the Serbs thought the right solution for Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, if we could turn back a moment to the Maksimovic diary and to an entry of March 18th, 1991, which may be found at tab 20 on pages 10 and 11.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is again a meeting of the SDS council on the 18th of March, and this entry, at the bottom of the page, the last three bullet points on that page read: "We have been talking for a long time about activating the National Council, but it is still not working. Shouldn't we forestall the declaration of an independent BH? Is it time to announce the joining of Serbian municipalities in BH with Serbia? We will continue with our parliamentary debates on BH -- will we continue with our parliamentary debates on BH and Yugoslavia? How long will we remain in the BH Assembly as deputies?" This passage -- I don't know if there's any more on the next page. "An appeal for Serbian unity is necessary now." This passage reflects Maksimovic's fears of, again, the way things are going and speculates on possible courses of action that the Bosnian Serb leadership could take to meet those unfavourable developments.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, beyond the contemplation of the separation of Serbian municipalities from Bosnia-Herzegovina as reflected in the February 23rd document and in the Maksimovic diary, did the SDS begin to undertake concrete steps to mark and separate territories deemed Serbian from the rest of Bosnia and Herzegovina? And in that respect, may I ask you to turn to -- or may I direct the Court's attention to tab 21 of binder 1. A Glas article referencing an SDS press conference in April of 1991.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, before we consider this document, let me answer your question and provide a little bit more context for this document. We have hitherto been discussing the -- what is the leitmotif in SDS policy, that is, the desire to keep all the Serbs in Bosnia within Yugoslavia, or at least within the same state with all the other Serbs. There was also a current of opinion, not only within the SDS but including members of the SDS, that the structure of governance within BH below the republic level should be changed. I have referred earlier and we have seen mention made in a couple of documents to the desire to re-draw municipal boundaries in a sense more favourable to the Serbs. There was also a desire, particularly, it seems, in Bosnian Krajina and in Eastern Herzegovina, to form regional governments, that is, a level of government intermediate between the municipalities and the republic. Regional governments which would unite municipalities in specific regions, distinguishable in some manner or another, to promote the interests of those regions. This was very controversial within BH, as I mentioned earlier, the SDA was opposed to any division of BH, any partition of BH, and this included any such -- or it included opposition to regional -- any type of regionalisation that would not take place on an economic basis. There had been a debate on this issue in the joint session in the BH Assembly on the 12th of April, at which ultimately a resolution was passed requesting that municipalities not join this movement toward regionalisation that was being promoted without the approval of the government, basically. The effort to form a region in Bosnian Krajina was already under way, and that is what the resolution was directed at. This session of the Assembly was apparently rather dramatic. The SDS deputies walked out, fearing being outvoted, as indeed they ultimately were. After they walked out, according to the minutes of the session, the president of the Assembly, Mr. Krajisnik, basically asked for a vote of confidence by the remaining deputies in himself, that is, he basically offered his resignation. There was some discussion, apparently. This is again according to the minutes. He eventually withdrew his offer of resignation, and the resolution was passed as a -- without the votes of the SDS, as a recommendation to municipalities. That is, it didn't really have any particularly binding effect. So that was on the 12th of April. Now, with a prologue, I think we can turn to this document, which is an article from the Banja Luka newspaper Glas, published on the 13th of April. And here we can see some of the background to the movement toward regionalisation. The article in question is a report on a press conference of the local Serbian Democratic Party, at which it was stated that the: "Initiative for regionalisation started on 21st January at a meeting of presidents of 22 municipalities of Bosnian Krajina," of whom nine were already within the -- what is called here the Banja Luka municipal community, that is, the Community of Municipalities of Banja Luka. "The final decision was made five days ago at a meeting of regional SDS councils," as translated here. The reference to the Banja Luka municipal community is a reference to a Community of Municipalities of Banja Luka, which is a form of cooperation among municipalities recognised with -- by the BH constitution of 1974. The purpose of this cooperation would be to promote common interests, economic interests primarily, tourism, that sort of thing. However, these communities of municipalities were not levels of government per say. They were not, in the Yugoslav terminology, socio-political communities. They did -- they could not make laws, and that type of thing. They were merely voluntary associations of the municipalities that belonged to them. And what was happening at this point is that there was a move to transform the Community of Municipalities of Banja Luka into a Community of Municipalities of Bosnian Krajina, with somewhat different powers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it correct, just to put this -- the beginnings of this form of regionalisation into context, that shortly thereafter a large rally was held, also in Banja Luka, during which members of the SDA charged that this was simply an effort at homogenisation of regions of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As we will see in another newspaper article, the SDS took such -- the SDA took such a position and held its own mass meeting in Banja Luka --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure of the exact date. Shortly before the 22nd of April, obviously.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The article concerning that rally can be found at tab 22.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at the first page, Mr. Treanor, I believe that indicates that the rally was estimated at 30.000 to 50.000 people, and then a much higher estimate, apparently, from the organisers of the rally. And if we could look at page 3 of the English translation, as it appears on your screen at the moment, perhaps we could see some of the perceptions of the members of the SDA about these burgeoning efforts toward regionalisation.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Many prominent members of the SDA were present, including Alija Izetbegovic. Here we have Midhat Ajanovic, stating that: "The immediate reason for our gathering here is the rash decisions on regionalisation, which are nothing other than attempts at national homogenisation of ethnic groups." And after him, Rusmir Mahmutcehajic spoke and is quoted as saying: "Today, outside BH, they want to tear up Bosnia and Herzegovina. That's why it needs to be said that this people in the heart of Banja Luka is telling everyone: That's never going to happen."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that same rally, did Alija Izetbegovic address the effect of efforts toward ethnic homogenisation in an ethnically diverse republic?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. I think we have a quote which will illustrate that. Mr. Izetbegovic is quoted as saying: "He who says that there are 51 per cent Serbs here and that therefore it is a Serbian municipality is not thinking well. Such a person does not mean well, for what about the 49 per cent of Muslims and Croats? To whom do they belong? Bosnia is ethnically mixed, and there can be no division here, unless someone wants disorder and bloodshed, and we don't want that." So here we see the position of the SDA expressed against any partition of Bosnia and their perception that the move toward regionalisation as being undertaken in Banja Luka at this time is a -- was step in that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you not to forget the suggestion of Mr. Stewart to make a clear reference to where we find it, because we now, without saying, we moved back from page 3 to page 2 in the middle of that. So if you would please indicate always where we are at that very moment, not specifically for us, but perhaps for those who have to read the transcript later. Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Within a short time after those rallies were held, Mr. Treanor, was a Community of Municipalities formed, and did the documents at tabs 23 and 24 reflect that?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. The key date here seems to be the 29th of April, 1991, at which a meeting was held in Banja Luka which inaugurated the new Community of Municipalities of Bosnian Krajina. I think the first document we have is the agreement on the formation of that Community of Municipalities. This is basically an agreement entered into by the municipalities that wished to join it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if we turn to page 3 -- excuse me. If we turn to page 3 of the English translation of the agreement, Article 9 of the agreement, can you tell us the significance of the provisions with respect to All People's Defence.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Looking at Article 9 of the agreement, we can see that the -- this new Community of Municipalities is assigning itself important functions in the area of national defence, including, for instance, in time of war, or under imminent threat of war, to organise All People's Defence in the territory of the Community of Municipalities. These types of powers were not foreseen by the constitution of BH for communities of municipalities, so this article in the agreement sets this Community of Municipalities out as being of a different -- in a different order from the ones that had existed before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you also a clarification. Article 9 is the only one who appears as a quote. Is that a mistake or is that - at least in the English translation - or has it any specific meaning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is in quotation marks in the original as well. For what reason, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, looking at tab 24, is a similar provision with respect to defence, found in the statute of the Association of Municipalities.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. If I could interrupt, Mr. Tieger. Your Honour, I do have a copy of another version of this agreement, and the version -- the second version that I have in fact bears the signatures and seals of many of the, if not all, of the 17 municipalities that are adhering to this agreement. And in that version, there are no quotation marks in Article 9.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So it might still be a mistake.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just looking quickly at the statute of the Association of Municipalities, found at tab 24, in particular at Article 16, which is found at page 5 of the English translation, does that reflect a similar focus on the defence issue and the assertion of the power to monitor and coordinate activities for defence?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I would just add that the statute is the document which sets out the purpose and the structure in the organs that are formed for the Community of Municipalities. And Article 16 states that: "The Association of Municipalities shall monitor the situation and coordinate activities for the organisation and implementation of preparations for All People's Defence, in accordance with the law, municipal defence plans, and the republican defence plan."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next two documents, Mr. Treanor, reflect the elections of the president and vice-president of the Community of Municipalities. Can you just tell us quickly who they were.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the 29th of April, at the founding meeting, Mr. Vojo Kupresanin - if we can blow that up - in Article 1 of this decision was elected president of the Assembly of that community. Mr. Kupresanin was an SDS deputy in the Chamber of Citizens of the BH Assembly. And then the next document indicates that on the same day, Mr. Radoslav Brdjanin, who was also an SDS deputy in the Assembly of BH, in the Chamber of Municipalities, was elected as the first vice-president of the Assembly of the Community of Municipalities of Bosnian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In the transcript the date appears as the 29th. I do not remember exactly what you said, because I see 26th as --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I may have misspoken. I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It seems that voting took place on the 25th and the decision is dated the 26th.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 26th, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, the next document you've selected is a document produced by the Deputies' Club of the SDS, entitled stances on the resolution of the Yugoslav state crisis and the position of Bosnia-Herzegovina in Yugoslavia. That document may be found at tab 27. I note you've highlighted a number of portions. Can you tell us about the context in which that document was created and the significance of the highlights you've indicated.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Getting back to the controversy about the status of BH within Yugoslavia, the issue was coming back to the Assembly which was scheduled to have a meeting later in June - and I can't remember the precise date - to discuss the issue of the status of BH within Yugoslavia. So once again, in connection with that occasion, the Club of Deputies has produced its own paper stating its position on that matter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if we could turn to page 2 of the English translation. I believe you find the top of that page highlighted, the first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here we find the SDS deputies beginning their statement on their position: "Faced with a dire crisis of the state of Yugoslavia, which is threatening to change violently the fate of the Serbian and other Yugoslav nations, Serbian deputies to the SRBH Assembly as legally elected representatives of the Serbian people hereby communicate to the Yugoslav and international public their stances, positions, on the resolution of the Yugoslav state crisis and the position of Bosnia and Herzegovina in Yugoslavia."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the very bottom of that same page, another highlight appears.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here we see a statement of their position, to the effect that: "No nation can be forcibly kept within the common Yugoslav state, nor can it be led out of it, in full or in part."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just for clarification: The use of the term or the word "violently" in the first paragraph, and the word "forcibly" in the highlighted section at the bottom of the page refers to what?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would take that as -- let me say, I'd have to speculate a bit, but I would take that within the context of all documents that we've seen to be a reference to the great fear of the SDS leaders and the -- their deputies, that is, the fear of being outvoted, that they would have a decision imposed upon them by the other deputies, a decision which they would have believed very directly closely affected the fate of Serbian nation and therefore one that they could not accept, a decision which, as Dr. Karadzic, I believe, earlier had expressed it, could lead to civil war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As a minimum, I would take that to mean having a decision imposed upon them by majority vote, by being outvoted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, if it would be possible to finish this in two or three minutes, fine; otherwise, we'd have the break now rather than -- but I can't see how many highlighted portions will still come.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I believe it is, Your Honour, and I'll hazard an effort to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, on the next -- there are three clips remaining, three highlighted portions remaining to be found at the bottom of page 6 and on page 7. And do those -- can you run us through those highlights quickly, the first of which refers to the solution of regionalisation, the second of which refers to the insistence on remaining in Yugoslavia, and the third of which suggests that consequences will flow from any effort to the contrary.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the first highlighted portion, we can see reference to the regionalisation issue in a very interesting manner. It states that: "In republics which have more than one state-founding nation, citizens and nations may proceed to organise themselves into regions based on economic, cultural, information-related, ethnic, and/or other interests. Regions, cantons, provinces, et cetera, may have certain powers in terms of legislation, justice, and administration and powers to regulate public utility services, as in some modern European countries." Now, here the issue of regionalisation is being very closely tied, and indeed directly tied, to the issue of the ethnic composition of the given republic. It only contemplates the forming of such regions within multi-ethnic republics, and indeed it takes as one of the criteria for the formation of such regions to be ethnicity. In the second highlighted portion, we see their view that: "In this respect, the Serbian people in BH are in a satisfactory position because they now share one state with other parts of the Serbian nation and can continue to exercise this historical and natural right. There is no way apart from brutal force in which the Serbian people in BH could be separated from Yugoslavia and deprived of the protection of their interests in the federal state." This is a reflection of one of the -- what the Serbs had originally regarded, the Bosnian Serb leadership, the SDS leadership, as one of their trumps, if you will, the fact that they were defending the status quo, that is, Bosnia was within Yugoslavia and they simply wanted to remain within Yugoslavia, and so it should be easy for them -- easier for them to keep it in Yugoslavia than for the others to take it out. That is one reason why they were so afraid of outvoting, because that, of course, was the way that that could be done. And then finally we read: "Any departure from the democratic way of resolving Yugoslavia's and Bosnia-Herzegovina's state crisis and diversion to a course of violence and imposition of one's will upon others," that's again a reference to the outvoting, "would entail a historical responsibility and other consequences that no one will be able to avoid."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we now silently move to page 7, the last -- previous paragraph, if I -- no. I'm sorry, I'm making a mistake. Where are we?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may. This portion of the document to which Mr. Treanor just referred is found on page 7.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The previous two portions were found on page 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have we gone through them, Mr. Tieger, at this moment? Because I think that both the technicians and interpreters, we really have to stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This would be an appropriate time, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would we return to this binder? Because we've gone through one binder now. I have the second one on my desk downstairs. Would it be wise to take this one and bring the next one?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Exactly right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for your guidance. We'll adjourn until 6.00 o'clock.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, if we could turn quickly to the next document, entitled, "What the Serbs propose," which is the first document found in binder 2 at tab 28. Is that document effectively a formalisation of the document you discussed just before the break, that is, the stances on resolution?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't say a formalisation. It's a dissemination of the contents of the previous document. This is a pamphlet which was published in both Serbian and English, the greater portion of the pamphlet contains the document we previously considered. And I'd just like to conclude our consideration of that document by saying that on the 12th of June, that is, two days after that document was dated, according to the minutes of the BH Assembly, that document and similar documents from the other Deputies' Clubs were submitted to the Assembly, but it was decided among the leaders of the clubs that there would be no debate on the issue. So that concluded that particular chapter in the consideration of the status of BH within the BH Assembly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we then turn to the next document you selected. That's found at tab 29. And that would be a transcript of the session of the first anniversary of the founding assembly of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. This is the stenographic record of the second assembly of the SDS, held one year to the day after the first assembly. At this assembly, reports were given on the development of party activities over the previous year. Dr. Karadzic gave an address, addressing, among other things, the general political situation. There was a lot of discussion of regionalisation within the party context especially, and finally, the Assembly elected officers in the various boards and committees of the party for the coming year.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we turn quickly, then, to some of the highlighted portions of that document. The first of which may be found at page 15 of the English translation and will simultaneously appear on the screen. First, Mr. Treanor, can you indicate who is speaking.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this point, Dr. Karadzic is speaking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in that selected portion, which is the fourth paragraph of the English translation, Dr. Karadzic speaks of slowing down and stopping the secessionist aspirations. I believe that's also found at page 16 in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can't see which paragraph it is on that page, but it appears to be in the middle of the page, basically the fourth paragraph. "In reviewing the achievements of the party over the previous year, we have achieved this: We have slowed down and stopped the secessionist aspirations that are still alive to this day and which will not be given up lightly. But they will not find it so easy to win and to separate Bosnia and Herzegovina from Yugoslavia."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the next highlighted portion found at page 25 of the English transcript, Dr. Karadzic speaks about the idea of regionalisation and its role within the aspirations of the SDS from the outset. Can you comment on that, please. And that would be found in the first full paragraph of the English translation, at page 25.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dr. Karadzic, according to the stenographic notes, states that: "Those who attend our afternoon session will be able to hear a part of last year's report, in which we presented a general objection to the regionalisation and territorialisation of Bosnia and Herzegovina after the war, which was carried out consistently to the detriment of the Serbian people. Thus, the idea of the re-regionalisation of Bosnia and Herzegovina had been present among the creators of SDS ideas from the very start and the Main Board has always taken that into account. All the ideas on regionalisation have originated from the Main Board, on regionalisation of the party, and others are also from the Main Board members." I have to say one thing. We have to preserve the strength of the party, not to give in to power-grabbing impulses and little Napoleons who are trying to do things to will harm the Serbian people." In this paragraph the reference is to regionalisation of the party, which I indicated earlier was abolished by the new party statutes, and there was opposition to that among many of the delegates to the Assembly who wanted to indeed see more powerful SDS regional boards, comparable to the communities of municipalities which were now being formed, presumably to cover the same areas. But Dr. Karadzic was opposed to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next highlighted section can be found at page 26 of the English transcript. And on page 29 of the B/C/S transcript, number 4, I believe.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Beginning with the fourth full paragraph on that page of the translation: "If someone violates the constitutions of BH and Yugoslavia, then we no longer have any obligations toward the constitution and then we will do what Messrs. Vukic and Kupresanin have announced. Not until then. Another party has to violate the BH Constitution, to try to effect the secession of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and if they do so, then we will prepare the democratic response of the Serbian people on all lines and in every respect."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the reference to Vukic and Kupresanin --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think the reference here is to the dispute about regionalisation. One of the arguments that Mr. -- or Dr. Karadzic uses against the establishment of powerful regional boards within the party is that the other regional -- the other party boards are structured the way the government -- the levels of government are structured. You have a municipal board and a municipal government, a republic board and a republican government. There is no regional government in Bosnia yet. The communities of municipalities were not, as I indicated before, regional governments. They might have had aspirations in that direction. Mr. Vukic and Mr. Kupresanin among such people, but they were not -- did not yet have that status, and Mr. Karadzic is not willing to see them elevated to that status until the time was right. And until then, he believes that the regional party boards have no place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the next highlighted portion, found -- before going to that, actually, let me turn to the next one in sequence, which is found at page 27 in the English translation, in which Dr. Karadzic again emphasises the importance of the local boards and the need to maintain contact through the local boards to the community. That reference can be found at the top paragraph of page 27.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dr. Karadzic is indicated as saying that: "And we keep saying that the main place of work for the SDS is the local board, the local board being the level below the municipality, in fact. That is where we are in touch with the people. We are not in touch with the people in the Main Board, but in the local boards, where every member of the local board has to be in touch with 10 to 20 Serbian households, to be their liaison officer in good times and in bad, through thick and thin." This is similar to the statement we saw earlier in the interview at the end of 1990, about the number of households that they were in touch with through their liaison officers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if we could turn to the next highlight. This is found on pages 29 and 30 of the English translation, last paragraph of page 29 and then continuing on to page 30. Is that a further iteration of the policy of not moving forward until steps have been taken by other parties?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here we see Dr. Karadzic again stating his view that it's necessary to go slow, so to speak, with the regionalisation process. He says: "I have to say here that the policy of the Serbian Democratic Party is not to divide Bosnia and Herzegovina until others bring it to that point. The SDS furthermore does not approve of the creation of new federal units before the constitutional and legal system has broken down. This cannot be done under our aegis. Those who want to do things that are not in the platform and the Statute of the SDS and the SDS views must form their own party. We had such examples in Banja Luka. A part of our Main Board broke away and created something they called the homeland front, not Kupresanin's front but some other homeland front." And to the next page, perhaps. "Which is doing stupid things, beating its head against a brick, pushing forward without any political logic and causing great political damage to the Serbian people." The reference here is to -- I believe to the desire of certain people in Bosnian Krajina and in Croatian Krajina to unite the two Krajinas and to form a new republic, if you will, of Yugoslavia. I might add at this point that this meeting took place, as was stated, on the 12th of July, 1991. Hostilities had broken out in Slovenia and Croatia after the declarations of independence, technically, I think. I'm not sure what the name is, but they basically declared independence, on the 25th of June, 1991. So the whole situation has now changed and we're entering into a much more intense period of political activity for that reason.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as we move on in the transcript of the anniversary session to the next highlight, are certain leaders of the SDS lauded by the party for their efforts over the last year?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Dr. Karadzic --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Treanor. I should indicate the page number in the English translation, which is 55 in that version.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: He gives some interesting remarks on the leadership of the party, and its most prominent figures. In this particular paragraph it indicates that he said: "We nevertheless have to name two of the delegates who have emerged as eminent political figures of their people, who are the flowers of the new emerging political leadership. These are Momcilo Krajisnik, Speaker of the Assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Professor Vojislav Maksimovic, President of the Delegates' Club."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, you indicated earlier the elections to the Main Board that took place in July of 1991. If we turn to the next two highlighted portions found on page 92 and 93 of the English transcript, do we see reflections of that election?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the first page, if we could blow up the middle of the page a little bit, we can see that Momcilo Krajisnik received 212 votes, which was almost equal to the total number of people attending the Assembly and, if I'm not mistaken, is the highest number received of any of the candidates. The candidates to the Main Board were nominated by regions, geographical regions, which operated for this purpose, to ensure territorial distribution within the Main Board, and the Main Board itself nominated a slate of, so to speak, at-large candidates. And Mr. Krajisnik was elected on that slate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Finally, the document shown on the screen now, located at page 93 of the English translation, is a list of all those elected to the Main Board on that date.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the list of the 45, now 45 members of the Main Board that were elected on that day. This is the official report within the stenographic notes of the results of the election to the Main Board.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, can I ask you to turn now to an intercepted telephone conversation between Dr. Karadzic and a reporter, in which he discusses regionalisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And Your Honours, the transcript is going to be found at -- excuse me. The transcript will be found at tab 3 of the intercept binder. However, this needs to be given an exhibit, as do the rest of the intercepts.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The CD containing the intercepts will be Prosecution Exhibit number P67, and the transcripts P67A.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And Your Honours, I indicated when we began the examination, we've made some effort to improve the visibility of the -- of particularly the transcript portion of the intercepts. Of course, we'd welcome any feedback from the Court, but we hope this will represent an improvement and make it easier for the Court to watch it on screen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, any comments before we move on to the second --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'd like to certainly comment on that. First of all, we've gone back a little bit in time, as the Court may have noticed. This is a telephone interview which took place on the 24th of June. That is the day before the events in Slovenia and Croatia that I referred to earlier, that is, on the very eve of the outbreak of hostilities in the former Yugoslavia. We see Dr. Karadzic reiterating the point that certainly as regards the Serbs in Croatia, it is not a question of any type of secession, but rather -- from Croatia, but rather, they are in Yugoslavia and they will remain in Yugoslavia, as their own entity, however. The project of Mr. Babic to join the two Krajinas is mentioned, and he says that he's against that for the moment, since there are no conditions for that, since BH is still also in Yugoslavia, and he would like to see the whole of BH remain in Yugoslavia. So this is a succinct statement of his vision of the situation at that point in time. The Serbian Autonomous Region of Krajina in Croatia remaining in Yugoslavia as a federal entity linked to the rest of the country via the territory of Bosnian Krajina, but Bosnian Krajina remaining certainly within Bosnia and Herzegovina and the whole of that republic remaining in Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honours, a second portion of the intercept to be played can be found at page 3 of the translation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here we see reiterated the same position, that as far as Croatia is concerned, it's not a question -- it's a question of Croatia leaving Yugoslavia, but not a question of the Serbs in Croatia, the SAO Krajina, leaving Croatia, because they're going to stay in Yugoslavia, because they're in Yugoslavia now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, I'd like to turn, then, to an intercept of June 20th, 1991, which can be found at tab 2 of the intercept binder. And can you tell us who the participants in this conversation are.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. The participants are Momcilo Krajisnik and Radovan Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor in the course of your comments about this intercept, can you identify some of the other persons who are mentioned during that conversation.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. This is obviously the first type -- the first such conversation we've heard, and I'd just like to observe that Mr. Krajisnik and Dr. Karadzic speak to each other in a very familiar manner. They use the familiar form of "you" to each other. There are several expletives in here. The exact nature of what it is Mr. Krajisnik wants to discuss with Dr. Karadzic is not clear, but it's clear that he wants to meet with him on what he regards as an important matter. And he indicates, in fact, that he has already arranged a meeting with certain other individuals on a different matter. And those individuals are Mr. Simovic, who is the -- or was the highest-ranking SDS designated member of the government of BH. He was a deputy prime minister. Also mentioned are Vito Zepinic, who was the deputy minister of internal affairs of BH, also a SDS-designated functionary, and Momcilo Mandic, who was also an SDS-designated functionary in the BH Ministry of Internal Affairs. He was an assistant minister, I believe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it correct that your report identifies two other intercepts, during which Dr. Koljevic and Mr. Mandic are contacted by Mr. Karadzic in connection with this same meeting?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There are a series of conversations on that day which all revolve around setting up the same meeting among the various individuals involved.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we turn, then, to the next intercepted conversation, found at tab 4 of the intercept binder. The portion of the conversation which will be shown and heard on the screen appears at page 2, or begins at page 2 of the English transcript.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Could you identify this conversation by date and ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Treanor. This is the intercepted conversation of July 8th, involving Mr. Karadzic and Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I would ask the booth for some assistance. We're not getting any sound. We'll need to start the intercept over again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, your comments about that intercept, please.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is the first conversation we've heard that directly reflects the new wartime situation that I referred to earlier. Mr. Milosevic is obviously very anxious about the military situation and is enlisting Dr. Karadzic's assistance, obviously willing assistance, in getting manpower for the JNA and various operations which are in planning. And Dr. Karadzic, in turn, asks him for assistance in getting weapons for certain of his municipalities, and Mr. Milosevic seems to -- or does indicate that it's not a problem. General Uzelac is being referred to is the commander -- or was the commander of the JNA corps headquartered in Banja Luka, the JNA 5th Corps, which took a very prominent role in the military operations against Croatia in the northern part of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, does your report refer to other intercepted telephone conversations reflecting contact between Mr. Milosevic and Mr. Karadzic, General Uzelac and others in connection with mobilisation and arming?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does. There are any number of conversations during this period which revolve around the issue of mobilisation, that is, getting manpower for the JNA to prosecute its operations in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, can I ask you to turn next --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you move to the next subject, Mr. Tieger, could I just ask you, Mr. Treanor: In the transcript, the words appear that something is of strategic importance for the future RAM. And then the question is: You know what RAM is. And the other participant seems to know. I do not know. Do you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do not know. I could only speculate from the context as well as you could.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, could we turn to the next document, which is found at tab 30 of binder 2, the minutes of a July conference on preservation of lands. Before we move on to the highlighted portion of those minutes, can you provide us with a quick overview of that -- the nature of that conference.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. And I'd like to preface my remarks by saying that these minutes are reflective of the new period in the organisational life of the party that I referred to before. We now start to get more minutes of meetings, in particular, meetings of large groups of officials meeting with Dr. Karadzic. This is, if I'm not mistaken, other than the Assembly stenographic notes themselves, of the first meeting -- the first such meeting of which we have a record. The title of the conference sounds a little humdrum, to say the least, but what is going on here is discussion of the issue of the ownership of property and the desire of the SDS leadership to prevent non-Serbs from buying property and moving into what they regard as Serbian areas of BH.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if we turn to the highlighted portion, which is found on page 3 of the English translation, does Mr. Krajisnik express his views on that issue?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. Mr. Krajisnik has indicated from these notes as saying that: "The main goal of this meeting is to be acquainted with the SDS action on land protection. Land around big cities is the most serious problem. These parts are overcrowded with men from Sandzak and other nations." Sandzak being a heavily Muslim populated area of the Republic of Serbia. "That is the reason why no one has a right to sell land and the other villagers should point the finger at one doing it. This is the most important task now."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we move, then, to the next intercepted telephone conversation, which is found at tab 5 of the intercept binder. And that would be a conversation of 18 July 1991. First, please, Mr. Treanor, if you could identify the participants.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is another conversation between Dr. Karadzic and Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honours, the portion of the intercepted conversation that you will hear is found on page 2 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Any comments on that conversation, Mr. Treanor?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. In this conversation, Dr. Karadzic and Mr. Krajisnik discuss a number of things, such as newspaper interviews, and so forth, and then they finally discuss, as you saw, the setting up of a couple of meetings. Now, the one meeting which Mr. Krajisnik is anxious to set up and have Dr. Karadzic come to is with people from MUP, that is, the Ministry of Internal Affairs. He says, "Our personnel." This is, I think, a reference to the problems which the SDS perceive as arising within MUP in the area of relations with their coalition partners. Under the inter-party agreement that I referred to earlier, the SDS would have been entitled to certain positions within the Ministry of Internal Affairs, including its regional offices. They were dissatisfied with the way this was being carried out, and in the -- beginning in the summer of 1991, this got to be an increasing -- increasingly frequent topic of conversation among the SDS leaders on the telephone. We saw the previous conversation at which Mr. Zepinic and Mr. Mandic were present, and they're the two leading Serbian members of -- or two of the leading Serbian members of MUP, Zepinic being the deputy minister and the highest-placed one. So this -- the one meeting, apparently, relates to that topic of the personnel issues within the Ministry of Internal Affairs. The other meeting with Mr. Lejovac - I'm not certain what the topic of that would be - but I could just inform the Court that Professor Lejovac was the head of the SDS political council, that is, its body of outside advisors.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to assist the Court in understanding the tenor and nature of these conversations: Is there evidence in the body of intercepts that Mr. Krajisnik, Mr. Karadzic, and others were aware that their conversations were being overheard and recorded?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes, indeed. Not only within the conversations, but there are other documents where they -- reference is made to that fact. And as we saw in the previous conversation with Mr. Milosevic, he had the same feeling, and there was another occasion, I'm not sure if we're going to be hearing that one, in which Mr. Milosevic asked Dr. Karadzic whether he had a secure phone, and they got into a discussion of the difference between secure phones in Bosnia and Belgrade, this sort of thing. But yes, certainly, they were all acutely aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The next intercept is found at tab 6 of the intercept binder. That is a conversation of 28 July 1991, involving Mr. Karadzic and Mr. Brdjanin. Your Honour, the first portion of that intercept that will be played begins at page 14 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before we move on to the second clip from that intercept, Mr. Treanor, if we could have your comments, if any, on that portion of the conversation.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, here again we see -- well, here we see, now I think for the first time in the conversations we're reviewing, Dr. Karadzic speaking with a local leader, that is, with Mr. Brdjanin, who is one of the deputies in the Assembly and, as we saw, is the -- at that time was the first vice-president of the Assembly of the new Community of Municipalities in Banja Luka. And he is trying to restrain Mr. Brdjanin's enthusiasm for, in this case, having a referendum, presumably to show that the Serbs want to stay within Yugoslavia and -- or -- I'm not sure exactly what the point is. Have Bosnian Krajina at least stay within Yugoslavia. And Mr. Karadzic is indicating that -- you don't need a referendum for that. They're already in Yugoslavia. And we have a strategy mapped out already for any moves that may be taken by people to take Bosnia out of Yugoslavia and we're ready, we have plans to meet that, so just please be patient.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to clarify our use of terms: I know you've used the term "local" in connection with local boards, being a unit below the municipalities, and we've referred to republic, regional, municipal, and local. Can you clarify, then, your use of the term "local leader" in referring to Mr. Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Very good. I was hesitating what to say. I think it would be fair, however, to call Mr. Brdjanin is regional leader. Without getting into the technicalities of what a region is, he was a deputy in the Assembly from one of the municipalities in Bosnian Krajina, but as I mentioned was also an officer in the Assembly of the Community of Municipalities. And I certainly didn't use the word "local" to mean at the level the governance below the municipality. He's one of the regional leaders in Bosnian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And I believe we just have time for the -- just enough time for the last clip of that particular conversation, which can be found beginning at page 16 of the English transcript, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, I'm reluctant to ask you to compress your comments. We're actually out of time, unless the -- so I leave it to the Court as to whether or not we reserve your comments for when we resume or take them now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you could do it in one or two minutes, we'd like to hear it now. If not, then we'd rather wait.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think we'd better leave it for Monday, since there's a bit of context to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, Mr. Treanor, I'd like to instruct you, as I did before, that you not speak with anyone about your testimony given and still to be given in this Court. We'll adjourn until next Monday, in the afternoon, a quarter past 2.00, in Courtroom I, this same courtroom. If there's nothing else to be raised by the parties at this moment, we'll adjourn until then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 23rd day of February, 2004, at 2.15 p.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
